t:
That the Fish and Wildlife Act of 1956 is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new section:


“Sec. 13. 

(a) Any person who—

“(1) 
while airborne in an aircraft shoots or attempts to shoot for the purpose of capturing or killing any bird, fish, or other animal; or


“(2) 
uses an aircraft to harass any bird, fish, or other animal; or


“(3) 
knowingly participates in using an aircraft for any purpose referred to in paragraph (1) or (2);

shall be fined not more than $5,000 or imprisoned not more than one year, or both.


“(b)

(1) 
This section shall not apply to any person if such person is employed by, or is an authorized agent of or is operating under a license or permit of, any State or the United States to administer or protect or aid in the administration or protection of land, water, wildlife, livestock, domesticated animals, human life, or crops, and each such person so operating under a license or permit shall report to the applicable issuing authority each calendar quarter the number and type of animals so taken.


“(2) 
In any case in which a State, or any agency thereof, issues a permit referred to in paragraph (1) of this subsection, it shall file with the Secretary of the Interior an annual report containing such information as the Secretary shall prescribe, including but not limited to—

“(A) 
the name and address of each person to whom a permit was issued;


“(B) 
a description of the animals authorized to be taken there-under. the number of animals authorized to be taken, and a description of the area from which the animals are authorized to be taken;


“(C) 
the number and type of animals taken by such person to whom a permit was issued; and


“(D) 
the reason for issuing the permit.




“(c) 
As used in this section, the term ‘aircraft’ means any contrivance used for flight in the air.”.

fable.w: The section creates a criminal prohibition on airborne hunting with an exception for state or federal permit holders, and requires states to file annual reports with the Secretary. The tempting reading is that the word "participates" or the state reporting duty signals participation, but "participates" refers to joining the criminal conduct, and a state's after-the-fact report is not consultation before a federal decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, explicit rulemaking, or right to sue is provided.
fable.s: it shall file with the Secretary of the Interior an annual report containing such information as the Secretary shall prescribe

opus.w: The section makes it a crime to hunt or harass animals from aircraft, exempts permitted or authorized government agents, and requires States that issue permits to file annual reports with the Secretary. The State reports are after-the-fact data filings, not consultation or coordination before a federal decision. 'Knowingly participates' describes the crime, and the permits are licenses, so neither counts as participation. Nothing here creates a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, an explicit rulemaking requirement, or a right to sue.
opus.s: it shall file with the Secretary of the Interior an annual report containing such information as the Secretary shall prescribe
opus.b:
I'd label this **No**. Two parts look tempting but fail the definition:

- **"Knowingly participates"** is just part of the description of the crime (taking part in using an aircraft to hunt). It is a keyword, not a process for outsiders to take part in a federal decision.
- **State annual reports to the Secretary of the Interior** do involve a party outside the federal government (a State). But the State is only reporting data on permits it has already issued. That is a compliance filing, not consultation before a federal decision. The phrase "such information as the Secretary shall prescribe" lets the Secretary set what goes in the report, but it doesn't clearly require rulemaking or a comment period.

The permits themselves fall under the licensing trap: applying for or holding a permit is not participating in a decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires states to file annual reports with the Secretary of the Interior regarding permits issued. According to the definition, reports to federal agencies are not considered participation. There is no requirement for consultation, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties before a federal decision is made. The interaction is purely informational and post-hoc.
qwen_chat.s: (2) In any case in which a State, or any agency thereof, issues a permit referred to in paragraph (1) of this subsection, it shall file with the Secretary of the Interior an annual report containing such information as the Secretary shall prescribe
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for states to file annual reports with the Secretary of the Interior constitutes "participation" because it involves outside entities (states) interacting with the federal government. However, the definition explicitly excludes "reports to, or notifications of... federal agencies" as a form of participation. Reporting data is not the same as consulting or coordinating *before* a decision is made. The section primarily establishes criminal penalties and reporting requirements for permits, but does not grant outside parties a role in the decision-making process itself (e.g., no public comment period, no advisory board with outside members influencing the rule, no right to sue). The reporting is a post-hoc administrative requirement.
